title: The Grace of Salvation
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The grace of salvation means that sinners are saved by God’s undeserved favor, not by merit, works, religious achievement, or personal worthiness. Salvation is a gift flowing from God’s mercy in Christ.
summary: The grace of salvation means that sinners are saved by God’s undeserved favor, not by merit, works, religious achievement, or personal worthiness. Salvation is a gift flowing from God’s mercy in Christ.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the gift and display of saving grace. Through His death and resurrection, God gives forgiveness, righteousness, life, and hope to those who could never earn them.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Grace is not God rewarding the deserving. Grace is God saving the undeserving through Jesus Christ. It begins in God’s heart, is accomplished through Christ’s work, and is received by faith.

Saving grace does not deny the seriousness of sin. It answers sin through the cross. God remains just while justifying sinners because Christ has borne sin and secured redemption.

Grace is also transforming. The grace that saves teaches believers to deny ungodliness and live sober, righteous, and godly lives. Grace is not permission to remain enslaved; it is power for new life.

Because salvation is by grace, boasting is excluded and despair is answered. The proud have no room to brag, and the broken are not told to make themselves worthy before coming to Christ.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people live trapped between pride and shame. Pride says, “I can earn this.” Shame says, “I can never be received.” Grace answers both by pointing away from self and toward Christ.

This doctrine is essential for recovery, discipleship, and ministry because people do not need a dressed-up version of self-rescue. They need the grace of God that saves, teaches, restores, and keeps.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Come to God by grace, not by self-improvement. Let grace humble you when you feel strong and lift you when you feel unworthy. Serve others with the same message: sinners are not saved by cleaning themselves up for God, but by trusting Christ who saves by grace.
